item.title: Chancellor shares vision for Millennial Campus amid ‘Save the Woods’ debate
item.description: UNC Asheville’s plans to develop a 45-acre wooded parcel have ignited an intense and ongoing clash with Five Points residents and other community members, who organized as Save the Woods to oppose what they see as institutional overreach. University leaders say the proposal is part of a broader strategy for growth.

item.title: Love & Sex in WNC: We all play a role in addressing sexual abuse
item.description: As a recent New York Times opinion video notes, around one in three girls and one in nine boys will experience some form of child sexual abuse, often from someone they know.

item.title: Pro tip: The health benefits of listening to different tonal frequencies
item.description: "Binaural beats are different tonal frequencies played simultaneously, one in each ear, and when the brain fills in a third beat which is not actually there, it promotes brain entrainment which decreases anxiety and improves focus, helps with sleep and creativity," says Tonya Harding, a licensed clinical mental health counselor.

item.title: Letter: Disappointed with plans for UNCA development committee
item.description: "We really hope we’re wrong, but this appears to be version 2.0 of a nontransparent, performative exercise that will exclude meaningful community and scientific input and accountability."

item.title: Pro tip: Screens hijack our nervous system
item.description: "Don't turn your phone on for at least the first hour you are awake," says Liz Roseman, an acupuncturist and life coach. "The screen hijacks our nervous system, essentially putting us into 'on/go' mode."

item.title: Letter: On board with making roads safer for cyclists
item.description: "I wholeheartedly agree that anything we can do to create a safer bicycle ride in the Asheville area is a step in the right direction."

item.title: Letter: Bikes and cars are incompatible on local roads
item.description: "If cyclists insist on traveling winding mountain roads, they either have to accept the endangerment or fund the creation of bike lanes."
